en:
I checked Heath and Jeanne's
health. Just as Valka
predicted, there were no signs
of the petrification virus
affecting them.
That's a relief! But I wonder\nhow it works?
They are infected, but I\nsuspect their bodies have\nadapted to the infected state.

However, since there's no
significant difference from the
Captain's genetic structure, we
must research further to find
the root cause.

Even on the Raza home planet,
there's no record of humans
petrifying completely. Usually,
symptoms are slight before
they return to normal.

However, as long as the full
extent of the virus remains
unknown, we cannot let our
guard down.

...And yet, we can't even settle
down to implement planet-wide
countermeasures. It's quite
problematic.
Why is that?
Currently, Raza and Ober are\nin a state of truce across all\nsectors.

However, the Raza Space
Force leadership, who should
be negotiating our future, have
all gone missing.
Apparently, they vanished\namidst the chaos of that fleet\nbattle.
That's quite unsettling...

We defeated Asmodeus and
Big Sister Eve is back, but
there are still so many things
we don't know...
Rekoro, is Big Sister Eve still\nnot awake?
Fortunately, her condition is\nstable, but there is no sign of\nher waking up.
I see...

Verda, Valka, and Henri are
using Asmodeus's biological
samples for a serum, but its
effectiveness has been
underwhelming.
While there are no signs of\npetrification, a full recovery will\nlikely be some time away.

Big Sister Verda and Henri-san
definitely can't just leave a
disease that erodes stars
alone.
I just hope the damage doesn't\nspread any further... Oh.
Good job, Big Sister Verda. Are\nyou okay? You look\nexhausted...

Mm... Tika, you're right. I might
have pushed myself a bit too
hard. Eve's condition just isn't
improving much...
Sit down here. Do you want\nsomething warm to drink?
Sorry... By the way, Coro, how\nlong are you going to keep\ndressing like that?

I'd love to get repaired, but
right now I have to allocate all
material refining to the
production of serum...
In this situation, I simply cannot\nreproduce my perfect, flawless,\nand marvelous body.

My own performance depends
on the ship's capabilities, so I
think I'll stay like this until
everything settles down.
It's depressing to see even you\nlooking so unwell.
Well, if you're fine... then...\nthat's... fine... ugh...
Verda!
Ah, s-sorry, Tika. I don't know\nwhat's wrong, my legs just\ngave out...
Verda! ...Oh no! She's burning\nup!
...Sorry, Tika... my footing is a\nbit...

Verda, stay with me! Let's get
you to the infirmary! I'll give
you a piggyback ride, so hold
on tight!
Gah! Tika!! No!! Get away from\nVerda!!
Eh? W-what?!
...Was I too late...!!
Coro! Get Mastima and the\nCaptain! Then, separate Valka\nand Henri from Eve! Hurry!!
...Rekoro, don't tell me... am I...
...You're infected.
Whaaaat!?
N-No way...!
Verda Kleiman is infected with\nthe Petrification Virus! Tika\nlikely caught it from her too!
This is an emergency! Summon\nLambda! Coro! Move it!
Y-Yeeessir!!
...Forgive me... Tika... I was\nbeing careful, but...
Don't talk...! I'm still fine! Let's\nget to the infirmary, just hold\non tight.
I'm sorry... Haha, so this is what\nthey call "carrying a child on\none's back."

...Sister Verda. It's okay... This
is a disease that has been
known for a very long time...
You'll definitely get better...!
I've just confirmed infections in\nTika, Ricardo, Karlyn, and even\nGiverese...
...What are we supposed to do\nabout this...?
Face reality. Crying won't\nchange anything.

...This virus's infectiousness is
abnormal. Isn't it even more
vicious than what the captains
described on Planet Roak?

Come to think of it... they
couldn't identify the
transmission route when my
father's comrades were
infected, either...

Perhaps the petrification
disease Coro knows about and
the one I know about are
different types.
Is there a possibility that Givel\nwas infected from the very\nbeginning?

Even if captured, they were
with Asmodeus, so maybe
genetic differences caused a
longer incubation period...

If that were the case, Valka
should have detected it the
moment they were brought
onto the Overman.

Euwin, Welch, and Lavarnia,
who were confirmed to be
uninfected, were evacuated to
the Overman.

As for Heath and Jeanne,
since they are infected, they
are currently on standby in the
infirmary.

Henri shows no symptoms, but
since he was present for Eve's
exam from the start, we
suspect he's in the incubation
period.
Kevin is looking after everyone\nright now, but...

If that's the case, then the fact
that we haven't shown
symptoms yet is truly just a
coincidence.

Exactly. In particular, we
cannot rule out the possibility
that the Captain is in the
incubation period, just like
Henri.
What is the status of the\nserum development?

The prototypes we've
completed are not working
effectively against Lady
Leash...

...Furthermore, we will need
specific serums for the Daftine,
Daftes, Levarance, and humans
respectively.

As for Lady Leash and Givel,
we haven't even been able to
identify their genetic
structures.

Can we not detect any serum
or antibodies from the bodies
of the Raza, like Heath and
Jeanne?
It seems their bodies do not\npossess antigens against the\nvirus.
It appears they are adapting\ntheir bodies to the presence of\nthe virus and neutralizing it.

Even if we were to analyze this
mechanism, we simply don't
have the time to apply it to
everyone on this ship.
We're backed into a corner,\nthen.

Can we ask Ober for help?
Asmodeus had already
mastered mass-producing this
virus and integrating it into
weaponry.
That means Ober should have\na wealth of expertise regarding\nthe handling of this virus.

How do we get them to hand it
over? We're still outsiders, and
all of Raza's leadership capable
of negotiating a ceasefire are
missing.

Jeanne Marswest doesn't hold
enough authority to be
delegated all negotiation
powers, either.

Besides, if a careless contact
triggers a petrification
pandemic in Ober, it will truly
be the end for us.
Then what am I supposed to\ndo?! We're running out of\noptions here!
Please calm down, Valka! This\nis no time to be fighting...

We have no choice but to
continue our research steadily.
If there is any silver lining, it's
that this isn't a fatal disease.

Kevin, Valka, and I―since we
don't have to worry about
infection―will take the lead and
focus on our research.
As for external affairs like\nsupplies, we can rely on Euwin,\nWelch, and Lavarnia.
Is that... really all there is?

At this rate, we don't know
when the Captain will show
symptoms. We must start with
what we can do... Captain.
Captain!? What's wrong?
C-C-C-C-Captainnnnnnnn!?
Damn it... it's onset!
Captain! Stay with me!
Captain! Please, wake up,\nCaptain!!

Even so, this is a blow... To
think the Captain, Eve, and I
would all fall ill with the same
disease and end up sharing a
sickbed... Hahaha...
Don't lose heart. For now, just\nfocus on resting. Leave the\nrest to us.
Eve seems to be in a stable\ncondition for now and is\nsleeping soundly.

Mmm... Sorry, but could you
keep an eye on Valka so she
doesn't start crying? She must
be quite exhausted.
...It's alright. Valka is holding up\nfine.
I see... You've grown strong...\nWait, am I being too\npresumptuous saying that?
Please get some rest. We will\ncome by again later.
Hey, Captain, Coro.

Ever since Eve left, Tika and
Mastima have fought
constantly. Mastima always
suspected Eve was up to
something...
Now that you mention it, that's\ntrue.

Come to think of it, I feel like
Mastima has been suspicious
of Eve ever since the days in
Daftine...

It's true that the battle in
Daftine over the Summoning
Crest was full of unnatural
occurrences.
Eve possesses the same power\nas Givel.

Therefore, it is not entirely
unnatural to think that the two
of them share some kind of
connection...

But... I just couldn't bring
myself to believe that Eve was
such a scheming, audacious
villain...
It can't be... Back then, Eve\nwas...!

You mean when the Captain
contracted Scorching Death at
the Levarance space base,
right, Verda?
...So, Coro, you remember that\ntime too?

How could I ever forget? Back
then, a cure for the Scorching
Death hadn't even been
established yet.
And yet, the Captain\nrecovered.
I could only conclude that it\nwas Eve's Gem Arts that did it.

If Eve were a villain like Givel,
keeping the Captain alive only
for utility... I doubt she'd look
so desperate.
If she could have saved the\nCaptain with absolute\ncertainty...

It would have been far more
effective to calm the chaos
and urge everyone to act
calmly to earn their trust...
Everyone was desperate back\nthen, wasn't it?

Indeed... Eve, who would do
something so irrational just to
save her comrades... she
cannot be a villain...
You're right... I think so, too.
*Sigh*... I've talked a bit too\nmuch. I'm going to sleep for a\nwhile.
Yes. Please get some rest.
...Truly, there is never a dull\nmoment on a journey through\nthe sea of stars...
Haaah!
I won't let you get away!
Take this! Hah! Get crushed!\nYou...! Daaaaah!
Alright... looks like that took\ncare of most of them.

I believe the number of
enemies defeated roughly
matches the figures predicted
by the Bazaar Council.
Hmph!
Ms. Welch, you seem quite\nworked up.
Even the Gem mining machine\nin the mine didn't react. She's\nin bad shape.

She's just frustrated because
she can't even go visit our
comrades who are suffering
from illness.
But the Stardust Bazaar has\nhelped Ms. Welch and the\nothers so much.

Thanks to everyone, we've
mostly confirmed the damage
from Raza and Ober's attack.
Dad will be happy too.
I understand that feeling of\nunease.

If I saw leaders abandoning
their posts during a planetary
crisis, I might feel like taking
their heads myself.

Besides, even if neutralized, we
don't know how the
petrification virus Heath and I
carry might affect the Ober
residents.

We cannot even descend to
the Bazaar. Euwin, Welch, and
Lavarnia have truly been a
great help to us.

Dammit, things should be
looking up in the big picture,
but nothing feels right. I get
why you're feeling restless.

With both the Raza and Ober
armies in total shambles, I
wonder what's going to happen
to the Azurite system.

An idle mind is the devil's
workshop. For now, we must
stay in this remote asteroid
belt and focus on pest
control...
Hm?
What is it, Boss?

Speak of the devil, I suppose.
We have a transmission from
Coro. They want everyone to
return to the ship.
I wonder what's wrong? I hope\nit isn't bad news...

I'm not sure if this will help us
decide, but it seems they are
about to leave the Stardust
Bazaar.
Eve has regained\nconsciousness.
What!?
Is that true!?
Yes. Under Eve's instructions,\nit seems we will be curing our\npetrification disease.
The destination is reportedly\nPlanet Lazuli.
Twinkling stars... become the\nlight... that guides him...
Nn... ah...
Haah...
...What the hell happened?
What on earth is going on... the\npetrification virus...

It's all gone now. I used the
Gems and my own power to
amplify them at the Urza Gate
to repair it.
How are you able to do such a\nthing? I expect an explanation.
I know. I'll tell you everything...\nRight, Givel?
...Do as you wish.
Eve... don't tell me, your\nmemories...
...Yeah. To be honest, most of\nthem were lost at Daftine.
So you admit it.
That's right. I knew Givel. Back\nthen, I let him escape.

Givel and I have never seen
eye to eye... In the end, we
realized we could never
understand one another. But...
...I couldn't bring myself to kill\nhim.

...And that's when I met Heath.
Heath, who possesses the
same Earthling genes as the
Captain.

I knew it. The reason Givel and
I disagreed so fundamentally...
was because of Heath's Earth
in the first place.

Givel said your goal was to
destroy Raza. And I bet you
don't even mean that literally,
do you?

You might not be entirely
wrong. More than anyone, I
wanted Raza to return to
where it belongs.
Because Raza... and Earth...\nhave vanished from the\nuniverse.
It vanished...? Are you saying\nAnother Earth has transferred\nout of the Solar System?
And how does Eve know of\nthis? Did you see it in the Urza\nSystem?
No. I... I've known about it from\nthe very beginning.

...From the beginning...? What
do you mean by "the
beginning"? What is the
meaning of this?

The beginning. Ever since the
Earth where Kevin's parents
were born became the planet
Raza...
B-but that was hundreds of\nyears ago!

Living a long time isn't strange.
There are those like me and
Mastima who live many times
longer than a Human in our
physical bodies.

Henri, Kevin, and even Valka
have lived for a long time
through the power of
technology. But...

Planet Raza shouldn't be Earth
in this universe... To have
known that from the start,
Lady Leash, just who are
you...?
When one studies Gems for a\nlong time, one occasionally\nruns into that very question.

No, it is simpler than
Gems―physics and chemistry. I
feel it in things that exist and
are established naturally.
...The will of someone, or\nsomething, that created them.
A "God," you mean?
That's a bad joke. It's even\nworse coming from you.

Demon worlds and lords exist.
It wouldn't be unnatural if their
polar opposites existed
somewhere in the universe.
Can you actually accept the\nexistence of something like a\n"God," Mastima?

God" is a concept all intelligent
life seeks. If scientific evidence
were provided, I would not
hesitate to acknowledge it.

...I see. But I've never seen a
God myself. I only know plenty
of loudmouths who act like
they're Gods, though.
Evelysse, what exactly were\nyou trying to do in this Azurite\nsystem?

...I wanted to prevent a
calamity that might strike this
universe in the distant future.
That... calamity.

After hearing Tika and
Ricardo's stories... perhaps a
planet that shouldn't exist is
here... that "two of the same
planet" exist in this universe...
...might have become the\ntrigger for the crisis, so I\nwanted to correct it.

...Don't be ridiculous. Even if
that were true, the Exorciser
should have been meant to fix
it.
It didn't work, and that's why\nyou lost to us on Daftine. Have\nyou forgotten?

Givel and I were in complete
disagreement regarding the
Earth that vanished from the
universe.

The fact that we couldn't
determine why the other Earth
vanished also caused our
conflict.

I believed we had to return the
vanished Earth to its original
place, no matter what. But
Givel...
If it is to vanish, then that is\nthe true history of that planet.\nWe must never distort that.
...It's as if you're claiming you\nhold the power of life and\ndeath over an entire planet.
But what you just said sounds\nexactly like that.

Speaking as if you hold the
entire universe in your hands...
You truly are a "pretentious
god-complexed fool.
He's right! I remember when\nEve-san brought a planet back\nto life.
Planet Berbent. Back then,\ndidn't Eve-san do something to\nthe entire dying planet?
...That brings back memories. I\nsuppose that did happen.
Berbent... The planet that was\non the verge of destruction at\nthe Pulse Tower, was it not?
That's right. On that planet,\nEve used a mysterious form of\nCrest Arts just once.

I don't know what power was
at work, but a single person's
Crest Arts actually stopped
the earthquakes shaking the
entire planetary surface...
It's true that my memories\nweren't all back to normal at\nthat time.

But deep down, I always
wanted to protect the natural
evolution of the stars and the
universe above all else.

Perhaps that's why the
appearance of the Thornite felt
like the universe was telling me
I was wrong,

and since I couldn't remember
why, the Thornite appeared as
a terrifying existence to my
eyes.

Even after that, every time I
traveled to a new planet, the
Thornite would appear just to
tell me I was wrong.

I didn't realize that twisting the
present to force a planet back
to its original state was the
real mistake.
Not until I met Heath.

Not until I saw the people
desperately fighting to survive
on the current Earth... no, on
planet Raza.

The "Earth" I finally found after
searching so long... I had
become an existence that
shouldn't have interfered.
Ah, I realized then that Givel\nwas right all along.

After seeing the history that
Planet Raza went through at
the Urza Gate... I felt like I had
to apologize.
That's why... I searched for\nGivel. But by then, Givel was\nalready...
Was he captured by\nAsmodeus?
...Yes.
...I'm not following this at all.\nCan we clear something up\nfirst?
What exactly is the relationship\nbetween Eve and Givel?
Givel is... my younger brother.
Oh.
Oh.
Oh.
...Now that you mention it, they\ndo have a similar vibe.
N-no, but that's... Wait, WHAT!?\nSiblings!?
This is even more shocking\nthan when we found out Tika\nand Ricardo were siblings...
I'd like to say don't lump us\ntogether, but... I can see it...
...If you're joking, that's in very\nbad taste.
It's the truth. As everyone\nknows, their personalities are\ncompletely different, though.

I feel like there's something
much more important to worry
about than their personalities
in this situation...

But if she was trying to save
her brother, it's understandable
why she had to obey
Asmodeus while he held him
hostage.
But why did she continue to\nobey Asmodeus even after we\ntook Giverese into custody?

She likely knew that losing the
means to summon Phantom
would lead Asmodeus to
spread the petrification
disease throughout Raza.
What?
At that time, all I knew was\nthat it was some kind of\nterrifying virus.
I can control Phantom, but you\ncan't do that with a virus.
So, to prevent him from using\nthe virus, I had no choice but\nto stay by his side.
In the end... it was all for\nnothing, though.

I changed my mind and decided
that I shouldn't send Raza back
to the original Earth, now that
they've begun walking a new
path traveling through the
Azurite system.
...But there were many people\nwho didn't feel the same way\nabout Raza.
Could that be related to the\nRaza leadership that is\ncurrently missing?
The reason I summoned\nAsmodeus was...

Because I wanted Ober to
defeat Raza under a strong
leader and seize control of the
Azurite system.

At that time, I needed to
organize my forces to return to
Daftine, where I had succeeded
in creating the Rift. However...
You summoned Asmodeus\nwhile you were weakened, and\nthen they betrayed you.

...That's right. Since the dawn
of their civilization, a faction in
Raza has always sought to
return Earth to its original
state and location.

Asmodeus always hated
humanity, so they conspired
with the faction seeking to
restore Raza to its original
form and position on Earth.

...They planned to corner Raza
with the Phantom fleet and
Petrification Virus, creating a
pretext to restore Earth to its
original state.

...I don't deny the longing for
Earth. The responsibility for
the post-transfer disasters
certainly lies with my foster
father and foster mother.
But even if we truly returned\nto Earth as it was in that era,\nwhat on earth would we do?

If we return to an age of
conflict and energy depletion,
the humanity that fought so
hard to survive will only face
extinction once again...!

...Maybe they weren't thinking
that far ahead. I think they
were just consumed by the
desire to return things to how
they should be.

Perhaps they expected
paradise to appear just by
changing the situation. ...Not
that I know for sure.

But wait, does that mean all
those people who are missing
now... are all holders of such
dangerous ideologies?!

That's insane! They're throwing
away our prosperity just to
prove this place used to be
Earth!
You're right. I was the same\nway...

...But I won't let that happen
ever again... and I won't forgive
those who are trying to make it
happen.

You're activating the Urza
System quite easily. I had such
a hard time with it. What is this
footage?
That is the Raza Space Force\nfleet.

Just fools obsessed with my
ideas. I think they used the
ceasefire to come and pillage
the Urza System.
Boss! Look at that! Could it\nbe...!

...That is... the
Commander-in-Chief of the
Raza Home World Defense
Force.
I know him. Until last year, he\nwas the Ambassador at the\nRaza Embassy in the Bazaar.
What is... that purple,\ncrystal-like thing beside\nthem...?
It's Grigori... A fragment of\nGrigori... There's no mistake!

That's Grigori? The thing
Bacchus D79 and the others
supposedly eradicated from
space...?

Exactly. This is bad. The people
in the footage have been
completely consumed by
Grigori!

Grigori parasitizes living
organisms, magnifying and
driving their desires into
madness!

...So Raza's catastrophic drive
to return to Earth is the result
of being infected by this
Grigori?!
It is certainly possible that the\nGrigori caused this situation.

Even so, there was
undoubtedly a desire within
their hearts that allowed the
Grigori to exploit them.
A desire to return to Earth, to\ntheir home, no matter what\nsacrifices had to be made...

Once again, the people of Raza
have succumbed to the pursuit
of power... Instead of relying on
their own strength, they
mistook temptation for a
blessing.

The enemy fleet has deployed
above planet Lazuli! I'm
detecting abnormal energy
readings!

...I can see that. Those people
in the footage... their readings
are because they've been
infested by the Grigori...

Even hearing about it from so
far away makes me sick. And
the stench of those Crests is
so bad, I feel like my nose is
going to fall off.
Humans... turned into that... Is\nthis really happening right\nnow!?

Stop whining about what's right
in front of us. Make up your
mind; we've come this far, and
there's only one choice left.
...You're right. We can't just let\nthings like that remain forever.\nIsn't that right, Givel?
They obstruct the Exorciser\nand distort the universe. They\nmust be eliminated.
...Small, pitiful, and trivial\nfragments of will, possessed by\nthe desire to seek their home...

It was proven long ago that
something like the Grigori has
no impact on the rightful
evolution of this universe.
...We shall eliminate them. For\nthe sake of the universe's\nfuture.
Abnormal energy readings!\nThey're descending!

If they're coming, let 'em come!!
I'll never forgive anyone who
threatens my home... the
Azurite system!
Those possessed by Grigori\ncan never truly return to who\nthey were, can they?
I don't know how much of their\nhumanity was left...

But because these bastards
hid their pathetic ambitions, so
many people who should've
lived ended up dead.
I can't bring myself to feel any\nsympathy for them.
Is it really over now? The war\nin the Azurite System, and\nEve's battle...
No, there's still something\nimportant left to do.

We have to ensure that things
like Grigori and Thornite never
disturb the peace of the living
in this universe again...

We must make sure that the
people of Raza and Ober
cannot approach the Urza
System.

Captain! Emergency! Fleets
from both the Raza Space
Force and the Ober Space
Force are approaching Lazuli!
What!? Why!?

The war isn't over. They
probably saw the Grigori fleet
approaching Lazuli and mistook
it for the enemy moving in.
Are we going to intercept\nthem? If you wish, I can take\nmy place on the bridge.
It's fine. This was all part of\nthe plan.

I had the Overman follow us
under the pretext of an illness,
just so they would be easier to
detect.
...What? What do you mean?
There is nothing on this planet\nthat would benefit either Raza\nor Ober.

On the contrary, I want them
to take back information
warning them that approaching
here is dangerous.
I want the fleets that fought at\nRaza's final defense line to\ntruly understand that terror.
...O, Brilliant Stars.
Become the light that guides\nthem.
Karnas, Accura, Eremia, Valena,\nDandelion... another Karnas...
Charles D. Goal, Diplo,\nAqualery... and...
Go... and protect the future of\nthe Azurite system... you\nphantom fleets...

So that people may never
again be tormented by powers
that deny the very lives they
hold dear...!
Phantoms that shouldn't exist\nin this universe... a phantom\nfleet, is it...?
Why not just have this fleet\ndestroy the Urza System?
That is my ultimate goal, but I\nwant the Urza System to live\njust a little while longer.
Because I have a promise to\nmy comrades that I must fulfill.
Eh!? What!? The Overman!?

Sorry for summoning you
without permission. Your
Overman is parked exactly
where you left it, so don't
worry...
It just happened to be the\nperfect size for me to pilot\nalone.
Alone...?
Eve, you're not going off\nsomewhere by yourself again,\nare you...?
...I'm sorry.
...Though, I've lost track of how\nmany times I've apologized by\nnow...
But this is something that only\nI can do.
You can't! You can't do that! I\nhaven't even forgiven you for\nwhat you did this time, Eve!
You haven't even properly\napologized to Lavarnia yet!
Hey! Eve! We're comrades,\naren't we?!
If there's something you have\nto do, I'll help you! Let's go\ntogether!!
...I'm sorry, Tika. But this time, I\npromise I'll come back.
Eve!!
Givel! Stay here and behave\nyourself for a little while!
I was wrong this time.
That's why I can't let my\njourney end here!
...Do as you please.
Eve... are you really going?
Eve...!
Captain. I've always wondered\nwhy I was on that wasteland\nplanet where I first met you.
Even though there are so many\nplanets in the universe with\n"Gates."
Captain. Do you remember the\nplanet Maere?

That planet was so similar to
Earth. To your home, that
wonderful blue planet teeming
with life.

Perhaps I was drawn to that
planet because it resembled
Earth, and that's how I met
you...
Maybe I'm overthinking it.
Captain! Stop Big Sister Eve!!

Captain. I'm going to pass
through the "Gate" on that
planet I came from, to fulfill an
important promise...
